title: Fix the mobile photo handoff test's generated filename assertion
scope:
Change only tests/mobile-photo-upload.spec.ts, case 'hands a captured photo to Photos Reel and reloads its protected image @mobile-image-orientation'. Derive expectedFilename as `S${session.id}_P${String(registered.id).padStart(4, "0")}.jpg` after receiving the created photo ID. The source file remains handoff.jpg; .jpg is its registration extension. Assert the persisted originalFilename equals this exact generated display filename, not the source name, a regex, or a value copied from the response under test. The physical object path remains upload.objectPath returned by /api/uploads/direct: do not rename it or derive it from the display filename. Preserve the backend contract in server/storage.ts atomicCreatePhoto and extension extraction in server/routes.ts. Preserve all other existing metadata and journey assertions, with no early returns, skips, weakened matching, altered fixtures, or auth changes. Require one successful direct upload and registration, registered.objectStorageKey === upload.objectPath, one persisted photo with registered.id, width 37, height 23, aisle B, section 007, and the exact expectedFilename. Complete the Photos Reel journey: active strip tab, visible photo card and thumbnail, src exactly upload.objectPath, successful protected GET to that path, decoded natural dimensions 37x23, and exactly one strip card. Reload, reopen Photos Reel through the existing phone navigation, and require a new successful protected GET and the same decoded image dimensions. Re-read the API and require equality with the complete pre-reload photo array, one persisted row, the same generated filename and metadata, and an empty offline queue. Confirm uploadResponses and registrationResponses still each contain exactly one response after reload, so duplicate registration attempts cannot be hidden by idempotent persistence. Execute all downstream image/reload assertions; currently they are unverified because the filename mismatch stops this case. This repair is independent of sign-in activation work; do not repair auth failures here. Out of scope: production changes, backend naming, storage layout, upload-security changes, gate maintenance, deployment, and separate independent verification. Any material production change requires scope reassessment and supported amendment before implementation.
